subject: Skyline: request to reserve dedicated model shard for enterprise pilot
messages:
From: Jamie Park <jamie@skyline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Pilot ask: dedicated model shard / residency for Skyline pilot

Marissa / team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The Skyline product team is excited to move the pilot to a production-like environment, but we have a firm requirement from our security and SRE teams: for the pilot (and initial GA) we need a dedicated model shard pinned to our tenant to guarantee consistent latency for peak inference (we run lots of short-burst queries).

Attached is our MAAP requirements doc — the key asks are:
- dedicated residency (no noisy neighbor on GPU instance)
- ability to pin a model variant for the duration of the pilot (4–8 weeks)
- explicit fallback policy if that node becomes unhealthy
- telemetry export with trace IDs for sampling

We're close on commercial terms (SOW attached) but procurement will only sign if we can get this operational guarantee or a documented exception. Can you confirm feasibility and a rough timeline? We’d like to close by May 20.

—Jamie
Jamie Park
Director of Product, Skyline AI
jamie@skyline.ai

Looping you in — this is an enterprise pilot that will convert to a $420k ARR contract if we can land the residency ask. Skyline needs a gating decision for the pilot by May 20.

Ask to product/eng: can we offer a temporary "dedicated shard" (per-tenant GPU pool or pinned model residency) as a supported exception? If full product support is too heavy, what's the minimum shim we can ship to satisfy procurement (explicit fallback + telemetry)?

Business impact: close risk is high; procurement has said no signature without operational commitment. If we can commit to an incremental patch or carve-out in the SOW (and an SLA for the pilot window), we can close this deal this cycle.

Please reply with proposed approach, approximate engineering effort, and whether a sprint slot this month is realistic.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Pilot ask: dedicated model shard / residency for Skyline pilot

Marissa —

Quick technical read: the ask maps to a few layers:
1) routing/isolation: need a routing policy that pins Skyline traffic to a reserved pool (dedicated instances or dedicated queue).
2) capacity: their peak profile indicates short, high-qps bursts; we need headroom or burst capacity to avoid queuing.
3) KV/prefix caching: to get steady low tail latency we should seed KV cache for the pilot or enable aggressive prefix caching.
4) fallback: define a clear fallback (route to shared pool with throttling + notify customer).

Workaround: we could provision a small dedicated pool (1-2 GPU nodes) and use a routing tag. That is doable quickly if infra can carve capacity. Engineering questions: is this a VPC/private deployment or hosted? The MAAP has a few network/KMS asks that could affect timing.

Estimate: if we accept a brittle shim (manual routing + reserved nodes) we can stand this up in ~2 weeks operationally (incl. infra provision, routing, and SLO doc). For product-grade support (console, rollout controls, audit traceability) plan 6–10 weeks.

Happy to run the sizing with infra if you want me to take the lead.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: dedicated model shard / residency for Skyline pilot

Thanks for the context. High level product stance: we can treat this as a time-bound enterprise exception (pilot-only) with a scoped implementation path. Before we commit to a sprint slot I need:
- clarity on the exact acceptance criteria Skyline will sign against (SLO numbers, fallback behavior, telemetry format)
- confirmation of whether they require VPC/isolation vs. hosted but isolated pool
- legal/ops acceptance for an SLA carve-out in SOW

If those align, I'm okay with a targeted engineering effort to ship a short-lived "reserved-pool" workflow and a documented fallback. That said, this will consume capacity from our infra squad — we need to prioritize versus INF backlog (INF-2345) which is scheduled this month.

Proposed gating: if this deal is > $300k ARR and procurement insists on residency, approve a sprint slot (2-week fast lane) to deliver the shim. Otherwise we queue to the regular roadmap.

Kimberly Park
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 07:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: dedicated model shard / residency for Skyline pilot

Technical note from infra: carving a dedicated GPU pool and a routing tag is straightforward from an infrastructure perspective if we can accept a manual provisioning + operational runbook.

Effort estimates (rough):
- Manual provisioning + routing tag + SLO doc + monitoring hooks: 2 weeks (1 dev + 1 ops to set up and support initial pilot)
- Minimal console UX and rollout controls: +4 weeks
- Full productization (auditable traces, VPC + KMS integration, tenant pinning lifecycle): 8–10 weeks

Risk: the manual shim increases on-call surface and we need an agreed fallback. If Skyline requires VPC/KMS for the pilot we need security review which could add 1–2 weeks.

If Sales can accept a documented pilot-exception in the SOW and a guaranteed fallback, we can deliver the manual reserved-pool in the requested window (by May 20) provided we reassign one infra developer from INF-2345 for two weeks. We need an explicit approval to re-prioritize.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Software Engineer, Infra

Subject: Re: Pilot ask: dedicated model shard / residency for Skyline pilot — decision request

Thanks all — to move this forward I need the following by EOD Thu May 13 so I can send a final SOW to Skyline and get procurement sign-off:
1) Product: confirmation we can accept an enterprise pilot exception with the following acceptance criteria: 95th perc latency <120ms for pilot traffic, explicit fallback routing to shared pool with throttling, and basic trace-id export. If product approves, note any console or telemetry gaps in the SOW.
2) Eng/Infra: operational commitment to stand up a 1–2 GPU dedicated pool and a routing tag, with monitoring and a runbook. If security review for KMS/VPC is required note the expected delay.
3) Sales: I will propose a pilot SLA clause and an expense credit for the first month to offset operational risk (we can discuss numbers).

If we can get an approval to reassign one infra dev from INF-2345 for two weeks, Karthik estimates we can be live with the manual shim by May 20. Please reply with a short "approve" or "decline" and any constraints. I'll consolidate and send the SOW.

Action items for next reply: product_approval (yes/no), infra_commit (yes/no + availability), sales_credit_terms (proposed).

Thanks — Marissa
